Article Title: Identity of 'Dimagi Naxal Party' founder remains a mystery
Article Text:
One Insta post states, "When someone says Dimaagi Naxal, all I hear is intellectual baddie!'

What's common to the social media accounts of 'Dimagi Naxal Party' - started over the weekend in response to PM's reference in his I-Day speech - and CJP protests is a high dose of Gen Z humour.One Insta post states, "When someone says Dimaagi Naxal, all I hear is intellectual baddie!'Its X handle @DNJP_India has amassed 14,000 followers, while a handful of X accounts have also added 'dimagi Naxal' as a prefix to their names as an act of solidarity. There's also a website with a manifesto and an anthem - which links to a YouTube clip from the 2006 Hindi film 'Rang De Basanti' featuring the actors reciting the revolutionary poem 'Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna'.Following PM's remarks, Congress' P Chidambaram called himself a 'proud dimagi Naxal' in a post on X, while actor Prakash Raj posted a reel urging people to become 'dimaagi' and not 'bewakoof'. Union minister Kiren Rijiju clarified that the term was not directed at opposition, and even came out with a three-point definition of who qualifies as a dimagi Naxal: those who support Maoists and reject Constitution, those who stand with separatists and support Article 370, and those who want to cut the chicken neck to separate the Northeast from India.While the identity of its founder (who is simply going by the name 'a dimagi Indian' online) has not yet been publicly disclosed, DNJP calls CJP a sibling party on its website. Its first tweet Sunday, "What if all dimagi naxals come together?" was also a hat tip to CJP's origin, which began with Abhijeet Dipke's now-iconic May 16 tweet, "What if all the cockroaches come together?"Unlike CJP, however, DNJP's 'manifesto' states that there will be no flag, no font, or founder doing press, and the only criteria for joining the party is a "functioning brain and a willingness to ask 'wait, why though' out loud". It is also clear about one thing: the deployment of terms such as 'dimagi Naxals' and 'anti-nationals' crosses party lines and is often used to shut down criticism."Every side of Indian politics has, at some point, called the other side 'anti-national' for disagreeing," the website says. "DNJP's bet: the people who actually think for themselves are scattered across every one of those parties - and a label meant to isolate them is exactly what could bring them back together."
Article Summary: 'Dimagi Naxal Party' started over the weekend in response to PM's reference in his I-Day speech. Its X handle @DNJP_India has amassed 14,000 followers, while a handful of X accounts have also added 'dimagi' as a prefix to their names as an act of solidarity.

NEW DELHI: India's star wicketkeeper batter Rishabh Pant created history on Tuesday during the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. The India wicketkeeper-batter became the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket.Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty.Pant became only the fourth batter in Test history to hit 100 sixes. Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes, followed by Brendon McCullum with 107. Pant is now third with 100 sixes, while former Australia wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist also has 100.Pant reached the landmark in his aggressive style against Kumara. The Sri Lankan pacer bowled a delivery on a length and angled it into the left-hander. Pant got inside the line and pulled it over long leg.Nuwantha tried to catch the ball but could only watch it sail over the boundary.The six also brought up Pant's fifty, his 20th in Test cricket.With the shot, Pant became the first Indian and only the fourth batter overall to reach 100 sixes in Test cricket.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant becomes the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket. Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty. Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes, followed by Brendon McCullum with 107.

Article Title: 'Voice sample is not required': Rahul Gandhi’s counsel opposes plea in Savarkar defamation case
Article Text:
File photo: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi

Satyaki Savarkar's deposition brings Godse-RSS links into focus

Case stems from Rahul's 2023 London remarks

NEW DELHI: The defence counsel for leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday opposed a plea seeking his voice sample in the defamation case filed by Satyaki Savarkar, grandson of Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, in a Pune court.Congress MP's lawyer Milind D Pawar argued that the case had not yet reached the stage where the defence would examine whether the alleged speech was actually made with a defamatory intention, and therefore a voice sample was not required at this stage.Speaking to news agency ANI, Pawar said the special MP/MLA court in Pune has directed the defence to file its formal response to the application by September 1.According to Pawar, the application was moved after Rahul's appearance in Pune on August 22, with the complainant seeking to have his voice sampled."A deformation case filed by Satyaki Savarkar against Rahul Gandhi. On 31st of December 2025, the chief examination of Satyaki Savarkar has been completed and thereafter on behalf of Rahul Gandhi, cross examination is going on," Pawar said.He added, "Yesterday the complainant has filed an application that Rahul Gandhi came in Pune on 22nd of August, 2026 and therefore, he may kindly be called for voice sample."Pawar said the court accepted his argument that the voice sample was premature."Still we are not come on that defence that whether we have really given that speech where our intention is defamation that defence is not yet to be came before the court and therefore at this stage voice sample is not required," he said.The voice sample plea came amid further cross-examination of Satyaki Savarkar, during which he made statements about the relationship between the Savarkar and Godse families and the latter family's links with the RSS.According to the deposition cited by ANI, Satyaki said, "It is true to say that my grandfathers Gopal Godse and Nathuram Godse were active members of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh."Satyaki identified Gopal Godse as his maternal grandfather and Sindhu Godse as his maternal grandmother. His mother was Himani Savarkar.He also acknowledged that the Savarkar and Godse families were related, although he said he did not have complete information about their historical relationship or whether relevant records were available in government archives.Satyaki said his mother died in Pune in 2015 and Gopal Godse died there in 2007. He also said that both his mother and grandfather worked for the Hindu Mahasabha until their deaths.The cross-examination also touched upon the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi in 1948 and the historical roles of the people involved.Some questions concerning the RSS and Digambar Badge were objected to by the complainant's lawyer, Sangram Kolhatkar. The court recorded that the objections would be dealt with at the time of the final decision.Satyaki Savarkar, a grandson of one of V D Savarkar's brothers, filed the defamation case against Rahul over remarks the Congress leader allegedly made about Savarkar during an Overseas Congress event in London on March 5, 2023.Satyaki subsequently approached a magistrate court in Pune in April 2023, alleging that former Congress president's remarks were false and defamatory and had damaged the reputation of Savarkar and caused distress to his family and supporters.The case is currently at the stage of cross-examination of the complainant.Pawar said the chief examination of Satyaki had been completed on December 31, 2025, while his cross-examination by Rahul's legal team is continuing. The proceedings were deferred to September 1, when the defence is expected to respond formally to the voice sample application.
Article Summary: Case stems from Rahul's 2023 London remarks about Satyaki Savarkar. Rahul's lawyer Milind D Pawar argued that the case had not yet reached the stage where the defence would examine whether the alleged speech was actually made with a defamatory intention.

NEW DELHI: NCERT has reconstituted the team tasked with preparing political science textbooks for Classes XI and XII, bringing together university academics, schoolteachers and its own faculty members, with the first of the two books scheduled to be ready by Nov.The 20-member panel includes faculty members from JNU, Delhi University, Ignou, National Law University Delhi, Jindal Global Law School, Pondicherry University and Utkal University, schoolteachers and NCERT academics, with at least four of its members known for links, past or present, with organisations linked to RSS or BJP.They are former ABVP national secretary and JNU professor Vandana Mishra; educationist Yadunath Deshpande, who has held organisational positions in ABVP and has described himself professionally as a BJP political consultant; Prashant Divekar of Pune-based Jnana Prabodhini; and JNU academic Ravi Rameshchandra Shukla, who has been associated with the editorial board of a journal published by Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini-linked Indian Institute of Democratic Leadership.The composition of the panel, however, is considerably broader, with it also having Prakash Kandpal and Ravi Shukla from JNU, Needhi Gupta from NLU Delhi, Chetan Singhai from Chanakya University, Sukanshika Vatsa from Delhi University and Satish Kumar from Ignou, among others.The Textbook Development Team (TDT), headed by political analyst and academic Sandeep Shastri, vice-president of Nitte (Deemed to be University), has been asked to finalise the Class XI textbook by Nov 30, 2026, and the Class XII book by July 30, 2027.NCERT said the reconstitution of the team was intended to "further strengthen and streamline" preparation of the two textbooks. The final teaching-learning material will be approved, published and distributed by NCERT.According to NCERT's Aug 14 notification, the team will work under National Curriculum Framework for School Education, 2023, and seek guidance from curricular groups dealing with social science, languages, Indian Knowledge Systems, environmental education and pedagogy. The books will also be reviewed for themes that include cultural rootedness, inclusion, educational technology, assessment and Indian Knowledge Systems.
Article Summary: The 20-member panel includes faculty members from JNU, Delhi University, Ignou, National Law University Delhi, Jindal Global Law School, Pondicherry University and Utkal University. At least four of its members known for links, past or present, with organisations linked to RSS or BJP. The first of the two books is scheduled to be ready by Nov.

Article Title: Paternity test of child can be allowed in marital dispute: SC
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Though the legitimacy of a child born during marriage is presumed, Supreme Court Wednesday held that a child can be subjected to a paternity test in a matrimonial dispute in which a man has sought divorce on the ground of alleged unchaste character of his wife and has claimed that he is not the child's biological father.A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale rejected the plea of a woman who had opposed a paternity test of the child. She contended it was a settled principle of law that no party can be forced to undergo a DNA test, and the divorce plea of her husband should be decided without the paternity test."If you are loyal, then why should you object to the test," the bench asked. It upheld orders passed by a family court in Pune and Bombay HC directing a DNA test in divorce proceedings initiated by the husband, who submitted that the allegation of unchastity could be proved only through a DNA test.In this case, the husband had privately undergone a DNA test, which returned a negative result, thus showing that he was not the biological father of the child. Armed with the report, he filed a divorce petition and sought a court-directed DNA test to prove his allegations."In the facts of the present case, to prove the prima facie case, the husband has placed on record DNA test carried out by the laboratory at Hyderabad which concludes that the probability of him being the father...is zero. Such DNA report obtained by the petitioner would form prima facie and sufficient material to conclude that the direction for undergoing DNA test can be issued. The second parameter is eminent need. The averments in the petition indicate that unchastity of the petitioner is the main ground pleaded by husband for getting divorce. A DNA test report would be of material bearing to prove the fact whether he is the father of son named in the petition.Considering the allegations made in the petition, it would be difficult to get conclusive evidence to prove such allegation, except the DNA report," the HC had said in its order.The apex court upheld the HC order, paving the way for a paternity test of the child."The petition is based on the allegations of unchastity made against the wife. Result of DNA test would establish the allegations in the petition. Therefore, in my opinion, the husband satisfied the parameter of eminent need required to be taken into consideration by the Court while passing order of undergoing DNA test," the high court had said.
Article Summary: Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale rejected the plea of a woman who had opposed a paternity test of the child. She contended it was a settled principle of law that no party can be forced to undergo a DNA test. A man has sought divorce on the ground of alleged unchaste character of his wife and claimed that he is not the child's biological father.

Article Title: Sumit Sarkar: The Citizen Historian
Article Text:
Professor Sumit Sarkar significantly impacted the understanding of Indian nationalism, illuminating its intricacies through comprehensive analysis. He explored the evolution of nationalism, internal disputes, and collective movements, while challenging conventional binaries. His focus on ordinary people's cravings for justice defined his contributions as a public thinker and citizen historian. This article pays tribute to his influential teaching and the lasting academic heritage he leaves behind.

Rahul Govind was a student of Sumit Sarkar at the University of Delhi. He has a PhD. from Columbia University and is currently Professor of History at the University of Delhi.

Professor Sumit Sarkar, widely regarded as among the finest historians of modern Indian history, was educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta, and went on to teach for 30 years in the Department of History, University of Delhi . While his scholarship ranged and roamed over the vast canvas of modern Indian history, some indication of the originality of his vision and the painstaking rigour of his scholarship might be gathered by examining one particular facet. There was a recursive quality to the way he returned to the question of nationalism in colonial India, its critique as much as its self-critique. One sees this in his early essays on the 19th-century Bengali intelligentsia, the path-breaking study of the Swadeshi movement in Bengal, as well as the singularly important essays on Gandhian nationalism.Sarkar was a Marxist historian and, it might surprise some that his scholarship was aimed at democratising the scope of nationalism, in terms of method as much as archive. Nationalism could only be understood in terms of popular aspirations and struggles for justice, be they about land, labour, dignity or representation. In the words of Sarkar, "what was remarkable [about the national movement] was the capacity for internal debate, change and auto-critique…combined with a persistent concern for mass poverty…and the need for mass mobilization [leading] to a progressive broadening of the meanings of freedom.One need only note that none of the four features central to the [Indian] constitution…democracy based on universal suffrage, secularism, elements of federalism and social justice through affirmative action had been present in the early programs of mainstream nationalism".His study of the Swadeshi movement in Bengal captured this complexity by analysing its radical agenda of complete independence, the rapid connections made between individuals and organisations nationally and internationally, the granular contestations over ideology, and the challenges of mass mobilisation. While Hindu religious symbols and imagery were employed by some for mobilisation, Sarkar shows us that even at the time of the Swadeshi movement, there was a recognition that such invocations of Hindu identity could be read in ways that reinforced narratives of Muslim tyranny or caste privilege.Sarkar documents the efforts made at the time to combat this possibility and to discover cult figures that would appeal to both communities, so as to broaden the scope of the national, with the revolutionary journal Yugantar suggesting a festival to honour Mir Kasim, not unlike those around Shivaji. Sarkar also discusses tensions within the revolutionary movement, including Hemchandra Kanungo's writings of the late 1920s, which critiqued the invocation of Hindu religious imagery as much as arguments of a Hindu golden past in the Swadeshi movement, since this was bound to exclude Muslims, valorise caste privilege, and encourage a cultic devotion to a leader rather than broaden into a mass movement with a political and socio-economic agenda.Kanungo could not be ignored: he was a legend even among revolutionaries, had travelled to Europe to study the technology of the bomb and meet revolutionaries, was imprisoned in the Cellular Jail following his involvement in the Alipore bomb case, and was deeply admired among fellow revolutionaries.While the Swadeshi movement was no doubt central to the formation of nationalism, it had its limitations in terms of its treatment of the communal and caste question, as well as its inability to adequately formulate a broader agrarian programme; these challenges continued well into the period of Gandhian nationalism.This complex and evolving understanding of the phenomenon of nationalism informs Sarkar's critique of theorisations which treat nationalism as captive to the rigid binary between India and the "West". Such theorisations of Indian nationalism, which value it merely in terms of its perceived indigeneity and difference from the "West", fail to recognise the evolving and transformative interaction between the two. Could one question Ambedkar for invoking the French Revolution in the Mahad Satyagraha, or forget Bhagat Singh's invocation of Lenin during his trial?The agenda of nationalism was broadened because of popular movements and local struggles by marginalised sections, so-called lower castes, "tribal" groups, Socialists and Communists. It is this historical and democratic expansion, based on ideals of justice and equality, that characterised the national movement and that, in Sarkar's analysis, distinguished it from Hindutva nationalism. He argued that important strands of the latter retained features visible in its early 20th-century formulations and remained open to critiques made at the time; he also questioned the extent to which questions of mass poverty or socio-economic change occupied a central place within it.Fiercely independent, Sarkar's Marxism did not prevent him from publicly critiquing in the strongest terms the Left government's policies and the events surrounding Singur and Nandigram.Sarkar, therefore, never shied away from drawing on his scholarship to speak as a citizen historian on what he perceived to be the crises of the day wracking the body politic. He was able to occupy that rare position of a public intellectual because his research attended to the fundamental questions that had a direct bearing on the dizzying churns of the present, soaring above the drive for narrow specialisation that can sometimes leave historians unprepared when it comes to addressing the most urgent challenges of the times.Writing this obituary, it is impossible not to remember his small office in which about six of us, privileged students of the MA, sat in 1999-2000 to learn, not Indian history, but the Renaissance and the Reformation in Europe.Professor Sarkar had his lectures meticulously prepared, written in his flowing, slanting hand on foolscap sheets of paper. The lectures lucidly brought alive the worlds of the Renaissance and the Reformation, and moved from Michelangelo's search for the perfect blue and the ambivalence and originality of Machiavelli's 'ethics' to the intricacies of theological dispute, showing how deeply knowledgeable Sarkar was about various aspects of European history.Amidst the gravity of the issues being discussed, on more than one occasion there was the unmistakable, almost child-like mischievous humour that would surface, his face breaking into a smile, the tone and voice assuming the sharp edge of an irreverence that is perhaps always inseparable from great learning.It was very painful meeting Professor Sarkar in the years of his illness, which he bore with remarkable and rare fortitude. Farewell Professor Sarkar, even as you remain in the gift of your teaching and in the luminosity of your works.
Article Summary: Sumit Sarkar is widely regarded as among the finest historians of modern Indian history. Sarkar significantly impacted the understanding of Indian nationalism, illuminating its intricacies through comprehensive analysis. His focus on ordinary people's cravings for justice defined his contributions as a public thinker and citizen historian.

Article Title: Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on Uttar Pradesh and 'Mission 2029'
Article Text:
Both Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani secured key positions in the BJP, while Amit Malviya was dropped from the new team.

Here are some highlights of Nitin's 'Nabin' team

The overhauled national team has 51 new office-bearers out of the 65 names announced, signalling a significant break from the past.

The new team has widespread representation, accommodating voices from 23 states and Union territories across the country.

Every major faith is respected and accommodated. The national team has one Sikh member, two Christian members and one member each from Muslim, Jain and Parsi communities.

The youngest BJP chief has opted for a relatively young team. Six office-bearers are below 40 years, 15 are in the 40-49 years age group, and 21 are in the 50-59 years age group.

There are three former chief ministers, 12 women and several experienced MPs in important roles

The committee has four tribal representatives from West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and the North-East, two of whom are women.

Special focus has been placed on the northeast region, with three regional leaders from Tripura, Assam and Nagaland and the continuation of a dedicated North-East Coordination Cell.

Focus Uttar Pradesh

Political comeback of many sidelined faces

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday hit the reset button as party president Nitin Nabin announced a new national team of office-bearers to prepare the party for the upcoming round of assembly elections, leading up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge. The party leaders described the newly constituted team as a strategic blend of seasoned administrative and organisational experience, youthfulness, geographic diversity and comprehensive social inclusion.The list has some high-profile omissions and some surprise comebacks. While Amit Malviya did not find a place in the new team after serving as BJP’s I-T cell head for 11 years, Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani made a grand comeback after staying on the fringes for long.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the newly appointed national office-bearers. "Congratulations to the newly appointed national office bearers of the BJP and those who have been given various responsibilities in the party. This newly appointed team brings together organisational experience, energy and grassroots connect," PM Modi said on X.BJP chief Nitin Nabin called his team a blend of experience and energy that will provide new momentum to the organisation and take forward PM Modi’s vision of 'Viksit Bharat'.In a post on X, Nabin said, "Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all the newly appointed office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party's National Team. With a blend of experience and energy, this team will give new momentum to the organisation under the guidance of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi.""I am confident that every member, with the spirit of a dedicated karyakarta, will further strengthen the organisation to take forward the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' and the commitment to nation-building to new heights," he further said."Such balanced appointments empower the incoming national president's executive team to operate with a profound awareness of the nation's vast geographical landscape and regional nuances," the BJP said in a statement.Uttar Pradesh, which goes to polls early next year, has been the biggest focus in this BJP reset. As many as 8 leaders from Uttar Pradesh have found a place in Nitin Nabin's team, the most notable being Smriti Irani, who once defeated Rahul Gandhi from his bastion Amethi Lok Sabha seat.Among national vice-presidents, Rekha Verma and Prof Tariq Mansoor are from UP. Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi have been appointed national general secretaries.Two national secretaries and two Morcha presidents are also from UP.BJP’s new national team marks the comeback of several leaders who were on the sidelines in recent times. From former Union minister Smriti Irani and RSS veteran Ram Madhav to former chief ministers Biplab Kumar Deb and Tirath Singh Rawat, several BJP leaders who had either slipped out of the party's top organisational structure or seen their political stock diminish have returned to prominent roles in the new national team.Smriti Irani, whose biggest claim to fame is her victory over Rahul Gandhi in 2019 Lok Sabha elections in Amethi, ending the Gandhi family's decades-long dominance over the constituency, thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."She described her political journey from an "ordinary BJP karyakarta" to one of the party's top organisational posts as "deeply humbling." She thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."The return of Ram Madhav, who has been made a national vice-president, is also significant.A former RSS spokesperson who was deputed to the BJP in 2014, Madhav emerged as one of the party's most influential general secretaries during its first term in power under PM Modi. He played a key role in the BJP's expansion in the northeast and was one of the principal architects of its alliance with the PDP in Jammu and Kashmir after the 2014 assembly polls.His influence waned after the BJP-PDP government collapsed in 2018, and he was dropped as a national general secretary when then BJP president J P Nadda constituted his team in September 2020. He subsequently largely disappeared from the BJP's organisational front line.The BJP later brought him back to oversee its Jammu and Kashmir assembly election campaign along with Union minister G Kishan Reddy in 2024.The first meeting of the Nitin Nabin's new team is scheduled to be held on August 22, news agency ANI reported citing government sources. However, its first test will be in early 2027 when several states, including Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, go to the polls. The BJP has a duanting task at hand in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party and the Congress together pushed it on the backfoot in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Meanwhile, with changes in the party structure announced, all eyes would now be on the possible changed in the Union Cabinet.
Article Summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin announced a new national team of office-bearers on Monday. The overhauled national team has 51 new office- bearers out of the 65 names announced. The list has some high-profile omissions and some surprise comebacks. Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani secured key positions in the new team.

Article Text:

Cavaliers land Peyton Watson in trade that sends Max Strus away

How does the 5-team trade look?

What the trade means for each team

Peyton Watson's restricted free agency finally has an ending, and it isn't the one Denver wanted. The Nuggets are sending their 23-year-old forward to Cleveland in a sign-and-trade that also pulls in the Clippers, Wizards and Kings, closing a standoff that dragged through the entire offseason.The Cavaliers gave up Max Strus to create the cap room, then locked Watson into a four-year, $88 million contract carrying a player option and trade kicker. In a separate but connected move, Cleveland shipped Tre Mann and a 2027 second-rounder to Washington for Cam Whitmore, with the Wizards forwarding center Julian Reese to Denver, who will waive him.Peyton Watson steps into a starting five that already runs through Mitchell, Harden, Mobley and Allen, giving Cleveland a projected lineup among the East's best on paper. He replaces a rotation piece in Strus and instantly becomes a younger, longer option at small forward.ESPN’s Shams Charania wrote on X, “BREAKING: Cleveland, Denver and the Clippers have agreed on a trade sending Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers, Max Strus to LA, and an unprotected 2031 Cavs first-round pick and a 2032 Kings second-rounder to the Nuggets, sources tell ESPN. Watson will sign a new four-year, $88 million deal to join the Cavaliers, plus a player option and a trade kicker.”The move caps a saga that started building in April, when Bobby Marks reported the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Brooklyn Nets were all potential landing spots for Watson. His market grew once teams realized how thin the 2026 free-agent class was beyond him, with Jalen Duren also unproven.Denver's return is entirely draft capital: an unprotected 2031 Cavaliers first-round pick and a 2032 Kings second-rounder that Sacramento previously owed Cleveland. The Wizards and Kings both play supporting roles, absorbing and forwarding pieces so the money and picks land where they need to. Cleveland's side of the ledger includes both incoming (Watson, Whitmore) and outgoing (Strus, Mann) pieces, structured to keep the sign-and-trade workable under the tax rules.ESPN's Bobby Marks laid out Cleveland's math afterward, noting the sign-and-trade hard-caps the Cavaliers at the first apron and that they sit "roughly $29M below the first apron" before re-signing Harden, who remains technically unsigned on a reported "wink-wink" agreement.For Denver, there's no easy replacement for Watson's two-way impact. He posted career-highs across the board in 2025-26: 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, a 59.4 true shooting percentage and a jump from 35.3 to 41.1 percent from three, all before a hamstring injury cut his season short at 54 games.The next checkpoint is Harden. Cleveland's cap sheet only fully clarifies once his new deal is finalized, and that number will determine how much flexibility the Cavaliers actually have left this summer.
Article Summary: Peyton Watson's restricted free agency finally has an ending, and it isn't the one Denver wanted. The Nuggets are sending their 23-year-old forward to Cleveland in a sign-and-trade that also pulls in the Clippers, Wizards and Kings. The Cavaliers gave up Max Strus to create the cap room, then locked Watson into a four-year, $88 million contract.

Article Title: Jason Kelce surprises brother Travis Kelce at Chiefs camp as fans swarm NFL star during special visit ahead of 2026 season

Jason Kelce gave Chiefs training camp a fun family moment on Wednesday, Aug. 19. The former Philadelphia Eagles center visited his younger brother, Travis Kelce , at Missouri Western State University. Fans quickly spotted Jason and gathered around him for autographs. He kept things casual in a white Mickey Mouse T-shirt while eating an ice cream bar and walking around the practice field.Jason’s visit also brought him back around several familiar faces. He hugged Chiefs head coach Andy Reid and spoke with players Harrison Butker and James Winchester. Meanwhile, Travis continues preparing for his 14th NFL season with Kansas City as the team moves closer to the regular season.Jason Kelce quickly became one of the biggest attractions at Chiefs training camp. Charlie Kirk investigation questions grow over SD card footage

Candace Owens is drawing attention to a tense moment in the aftermath of Charlie Kirk’s fatal shooting at Utah Valley University. The screenshot shows a post claiming that Candace Owens has released previously unseen footage involving SD cards removed from a camera positioned behind Kirk. Because I got to tell you something, Andrew, were it me and I was amongst my peers sitting on a jury, I would not accept your narrative that he looks like he's worried about people stealing. Her attention is on what she believes happened after that moment. Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I was in a really dark place. My family and my inner circle saved my life” - How Nick Kyrgios turned mental health battles and family love into tennis redemption
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “I was in a really dark place. My family and my inner circle saved my life” - How Nick Kyrgios turned mental health battles and family love into tennis redemption

How did Nick Kyrgios reach his darkest point in 2019

How did Nick Kyrgios’ family help him through his mental health battle

How did Nick Kyrgios turn his struggles into tennis success

What does Nick Kyrgios’ latest setback mean for his journey

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nick Kyrgios has never had a simple relationship with tennis. The Australian star has spoken openly about depression, self-harm, alcohol and drug use, and a period in 2019 when he was struggling to see a way forward. His family and close friends became an important part of his recovery. That journey later led him to an Australian Open doubles title and the Wimbledon singles final in 2022. But Kyrgios’ story is still unfolding. In August 2026, he was provisionally suspended after testing positive for cocaine, once again putting his mental health and personal struggles in focus.Kyrgios was already a major name in tennis when he began struggling badly with his mental health. His breakthrough had come at Wimbledon in 2014, when the 19-year-old wildcard beat Rafael Nadal in one of the biggest wins of his young career.The attention grew quickly after that. Kyrgios became known for his huge serve, unusual shot-making and emotional behaviour on court. He was also under constant pressure to live up to his talent.By 2019, he said he was not coping well with that pressure. In an interview later published about his struggles, Kyrgios described that period as one of the lowest points of his life.“2019 was the lowest point of my career. That pressure, having all eyes on you, the expectation, I couldn’t deal with it.”He also spoke about drinking, drug use, pushing away people close to him and hurting himself. After losing at Wimbledon that year, he returned to his hotel and found his father crying beside him. Kyrgios later said that moment made him realise that he could not continue living in the same way.He eventually went to a psychiatric ward in London. He later explained that doctors wanted him to stay for two weeks so his condition could be assessed.For someone who had spent years being seen mainly through his behaviour on a tennis court, admitting how badly he was struggling was a major change.In 2022, Kyrgios also wrote about that period on Instagram, saying he had been lonely, depressed and struggling to get out of bed while still having to play in front of millions of people. The Guardian reported his comments at the time.Kyrgios has repeatedly spoken about the importance of his family and the people closest to him. His struggles became worse when he began shutting them out, something he later recognised as part of the problem.His father, Giorgos, was with him during the difficult period in 2019. That night after the Wimbledon defeat became especially important because seeing his father break down forced Kyrgios to look at what was happening to him.“I lost at Wimbledon, I woke up and my dad was just sitting next to me on the bed and he was like full-blown crying. That was a bit wake-up call for me. I was like, okay, I cannot keep doing this.”His relationship with his family has remained a major part of how he talks about his life away from tennis.Kyrgios has also spoken about how difficult fame was for his family when his career suddenly took off. In an interview with Ed Mylett, he explained that he and his family came from a quiet area in Canberra and were not wealthy. Success changed their lives quickly, and he said they were not prepared for that level of attention.He also said that spending more time with his family during injury breaks helped him understand how much he had missed them while travelling around the tennis world.That support became even more important as Kyrgios dealt with injuries and the long periods away from competition that followed his biggest season.The clearest sign that Kyrgios had found a better balance came in 2022.He teamed up with his childhood friend Thanasi Kokkinakis at the Australian Open. The pair entered the men’s doubles tournament as wildcards and went on to win the title, beating fellow Australians Matthew Ebden and Max Purcell in the final. It was the first Australian men’s doubles title at the tournament since 1997.Only months later, Kyrgios reached the Wimbledon singles final.That run was one of the biggest achievements of his career. He beat several strong opponents before meeting Novak Djokovic in the final. Kyrgios won the opening set but Djokovic came back to win 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 7-6(3).The result still marked a major change for Kyrgios. He had gone from speaking publicly about suicidal thoughts and severe mental health struggles to playing in his first Grand Slam singles final.After the final, Kyrgios spoke about the pressure he had felt throughout the tournament.“It’s just a lot mentally. Everyone’s supporting you. There are negative comments. Like the pressure of playing finals at Wimbledon.”He also described the strange feeling of being on Centre Court after everything he had experienced.“I’m just not supposed to be here. Like, I’m a kid from Canberra.”Those words captured why his Wimbledon run meant more than simply reaching a final. It showed how much his life had changed.Kyrgios’ story cannot be described as a straight line from struggle to recovery. His recent years have included serious injuries, limited time on court and renewed personal difficulties.In August 2026, the International Tennis Integrity Agency provisionally suspended him after he tested positive for cocaine at an ATP tournament in Mallorca in June. The substance found in his sample was benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. Kyrgios accepted responsibility and said he had made a “huge mistake”.He linked the episode to the physical and mental strain caused by years of injuries and uncertainty over his tennis future. He also announced a 28-day break from social media and public life to focus on his well-being.That latest chapter does not erase what Kyrgios achieved in 2022, nor does it make his earlier openness about mental health less important. It does, however, show that recovery is not always a straight path.Kyrgios has spent much of his career being judged for what people see on the court. His own accounts have shown that there was always much more happening away from it. His willingness to talk about depression, self-harm, substance use and the role of his family has given fans a different way to understand him.His tennis story includes a Wimbledon final and a Grand Slam doubles title. His personal story is more complicated. It is about asking for help, accepting support, falling back into difficult places and trying to find a way forward again.
Article Summary: Tennis star Nick Kyrgios has struggled with mental health in recent years. He has spoken openly about depression, self-harm, alcohol and drug use. His family and close friends became an important part of his recovery. That journey led him to an Australian Open doubles title and the Wimbledon singles final in 2022. In August 2026, he was provisionally suspended after testing positive for cocaine.

He spent 13 seasons as an NFL center with the Eagles and became one of the league’s most respected offensive linemen before retiring after the 2023 season.The NFL Network schedule creates an interesting opportunity for Kelce. Kelce can offer technical football analysis without losing the conversational quality that has become central to his television persona.Still, nothing is settled. The report makes clear that Kelce’s role remains undecided, meaning the final NFL Network booths could look different once ESPN completes its plans.For now, the possibility alone adds another intriguing chapter to Jason Kelce’s post-NFL career. The former Eagles star has already proven he can command attention away from the field. A spot in the booth would give him another opportunity to show whether that appeal can translate to live NFL game coverage.

Article Title: How could Patrick Mahomes’ $43.56M restructure help the Chiefs make another bold move? Here’s what could come next
Article Text:
How could Patrick Mahomes’ $43.56M restructure help the Chiefs make another bold move? Here’s what could come next (Via X)

General Manager Chris Shea confirms the Chiefs could make another move before Week 1

The Kansas City Chiefs have less than $4 million in effective salary-cap space, but that number may not stay there for long. Patrick Mahomes already helped the team create $43.56 million in room with his latest restructure. Now, assistant general manager Chris Shea has confirmed that Kansas City has more ways to create flexibility before the 2026 regular season. That could give Brett Veach another chance to improve the roster.The Chiefs entered the 2026 offseason nearly $60 million over the salary cap. They have since cleared significant money through contract changes and roster decisions. Still, Kansas City has not closed the door on another move. With the final roster taking shape, the front office has several ways to make more room if it sees a player worth adding.Mahomes gave Kansas City its biggest cap boost on Feb. 18. The Chiefs converted $44.05 million of his base salary and a $10.4 million roster bonus into a signing bonus. The move created $43.56 million in 2026 cap space and reduced Mahomes’ 2026 cap hit to $34.65 million.It marked the fifth restructure of Mahomes’ NFL career. The move also showed how strongly Kansas City wants to keep adding pieces around its franchise quarterback.The Chiefs did more than restructure Mahomes’ deal. They released Jawaan Taylor and Mike Danna, clearing about $29 million, while Drue Tranquill agreed to a pay cut worth more than $2 million. Trey Smith had also restructured his contract the previous year, creating another $735,000 in cap room.That history gives Veach and Shea plenty of options. The Chiefs can restructure another veteran contract, make a roster cut or use a combination of moves to create room.There is also a clear reason to keep some flexibility. Chris Jones carries a $44.85 million cap hit in 2026, while Mahomes sits at $34.65 million. Trey Smith, Nick Bolton, Jaylon Moore and Creed Humphrey also carry significant cap numbers.Kansas City does not need to make another huge move simply for the sake of spending. However, one more restructure could give the team breathing room for the regular season or allow Veach to react if a useful player becomes available.Shea addressed the Chiefs’ cap situation on Aug. 19 after training camp practice. With Kansas City sitting at just under $4 million in effective cap space, he made it clear that the front office already has a plan.“We feel good about where we’re at,” Shea said during his Aug. 19 press conference. “Obviously, the rules change a little bit when the season starts. Certain things come onto the cap that aren’t there now. You know, we have a plan to create ample space for us to be able to operate with those charges that come on and create some flexibility.“You know, we have lots of avenues to create more flexibility and more cap space. We may take advantage of some or all in the next few weeks, but we certainly have the ability and likely will create some cap space to get us into the regular season.”That final line gives the Chiefs’ plan away. Kansas City will likely create more room before the regular season starts.The team also has another advantage during roster cuts. After finishing 6-11 in 2025, the Chiefs hold the eighth waiver priority, their best position in years. Assistant GM Mike Bradway said on Aug. 19 that the team remains open to waiver claims and trades during the roster-cut process.So, another Chiefs move does not necessarily mean a blockbuster signing. It could mean clearing enough money to claim a player, complete a trade or handle regular-season charges without financial pressure.Mahomes already did his part in February. Now Veach and Shea have the tools to make another move if the right opportunity appears.
Article Summary: Kansas City Chiefs have less than $4 million in effective salary-cap space. Patrick Mahomes’ $43.56M restructure gives the Chiefs another route to create cap space. General Manager Chris Shea confirms the Chiefs could make another move before Week 1.

Article Title: "No intent to return her": Former UFC star Chuck Liddell claims ex-wife abducted 14-year-old daughter amid custody battle
Article Text:
Chuck Liddell and his now-ex-wife Heidi Northcott. Image via: Getty Images

Chuck Liddell claims ex-wife abducted their 14-year-old daughter

Heidi Northcott reacts to Chuck Liddell's claims

Former UFC star Chuck Liddell has accused his ex-wife Heidi Northcott of abducting their 14-year-old daughter, Guinevere, and has asked a Los Angeles court to grant him full custody of the teenager. Liddell filed an emergency custody order this week, claiming Northcott took Guinevere to Orange County during his custodial week and against existing court orders.The dispute comes just as Guinevere was due to begin her first year of high school. Liddell says the situation could disrupt her education and volleyball season, while also creating further stress for her younger brother, 13-year-old Charlie. A court hearing on the custody request is scheduled for Aug. 24.According to Chuck Liddell's emergency filing, the dispute escalated after Northcott's efforts to secure court permission to move both children to Newport Beach did not succeed before the new school year. He alleges she then took Guinevere from his home last Thursday, during his custodial week, and moved her to Orange County.Liddell claims Northcott violated several custody-related orders in the process.He says she stopped using the court-approved co-parenting communication app, used the children as messengers, failed to bring Guinevere to extracurricular activities and did not follow the existing custody schedule. He further alleges she took their daughter with "no intent to return her."The former UFC champion told the court he is concerned about the impact on Guinevere if she misses the opening week of high school. He cited the possibility that she could lose her place on the volleyball team after making the squad during summer tryouts.Liddell also raised concerns about the effect on Charlie, saying the siblings are very close. He argued that separating them has created "instability and chaos for both" children and described the situation as a source of significant emotional and physical strain.Liddell is asking the court to give him sole physical custody of both children until the matter can be formally heard. He has also requested that Northcott's visitation be monitored, arguing that restrictions are needed to prevent what he describes as further manipulation, another removal of the children or attempts to alienate them from him.Northcott has denied Liddell's allegations while offering a different account of what happened. She told TMZ that she never abducted Guinevere and claimed the teenager "begged" her to take her from her father's home.Northcott also accused Liddell of trying to control her since their divorce. "For the past 5 years after our divorce, Chuck has been obsessed with staying in my life and trying to control me," she said. She added that their children "don't feel safe speaking up to him at this point."The custody dispute follows a lengthy divorce battle. Liddell and Northcott married in 2011 and finalized their divorce in April 2025, nearly four years after Liddell initially filed.Northcott said she is "exhausted" by the ongoing conflict and rejected the accusation that she abducted Guinevere. "My door has always been open for my kids to see Chuck, and I never abducted anyone," she told TMZ.For now, the competing accounts are unresolved. Liddell is seeking an emergency change to the existing custody arrangement, while Northcott disputes his version of events. The next significant development will come when the case reaches court on Aug. 24.The hearing could determine whether Liddell receives temporary sole physical custody and whether Northcott's contact with the children will be subject to monitoring while the wider custody dispute continues.
Article Summary: Former UFC star Chuck Liddell has accused his ex-wife Heidi Northcott of abducting their 14-year-old daughter, Guinevere. He has asked a Los Angeles court to grant him full custody of the teenager. Northcott says she never abducted the teenager and claimed the teenager "begged" her to take her from her father's home.

Ollie Robinson gave England the start they wanted in the first Test of Joe Root 's second spell as Test captain, dismissing Pakistan opener Awais Ali for a golden duck with the very first ball of the series at Headingley.Robinson trapped Awais lbw with the first delivery of the match. Awais reviewed the decision, hoping the ball had pitched outside the line, but the review returned three reds and the decision stayed.The fast bowler struck again in his opening spell, dismissing Pakistan captain Shan Masood in his third over to leave the visitors at 6-2.After 10 overs, rain forced the players off the field with Pakistan on 19-2.Robinson has now taken a wicket in the first over of a Test innings in back-to-back matches. During his return to England's Test side against New Zealand at Lord's earlier this summer, after more than two years out of the team, he picked up three wickets in his opening over. He finished that match with five wickets in New Zealand's first innings and two more in the second as England won by 115 runs.The wicket of Awais also put Robinson into the record books. It was the first time an England bowler had taken a wicket with the first ball of the opening Test of a series played in England.He also became only the second England bowler to dismiss a batter with the first ball of any Test series. West Indies fast bowler Pedro Collins is the only player to do it twice, dismissing Bangladesh opener Hannan Sarkar.

Gali agar na chunta ye toh,Mujhko itna naam na milta.Is haseen mehfil mein tumko aaj na milta, kal na milta.Main toh apne bachpan mein hi in mahalon se rooth gaya,Maine path ko kabhi na chhoda, chahe kitna toot gaya.Roti ke tukdon se zyada maine apne sapne ko maan diya,Har pal — har ghadi, is din ke liye jiya.Maine khoob tarazu par chadhte dekha imaanon ko,Pashuon ke pairon ko chhoote dekha hai insaanon ko.Par jhoothe is sansaar mein ji rahe sab hain moh mein,Jab chahat toh kuch aur hi hai unki rooh mein.Main in rangon mein ghul jaata,Ya dhal jaata chaandi mein,Par sona phir main kabhi na banta.Jo tham jaata aalochanaon par,Aur sabhi kuch mil jaata,Mujhko mera ghaam na milta, mujhko khud ka maan na milta.Mujhko in phoolon ka, in jharno ka jaadu bharmaata chala gaya,Main bhi par inko ji bhar kar thukraata chala gaya.Meri toh keval hasrat thi duniya se takraane ki,Meri toh keval hasrat thi apna sapna ji jaane ki.Main mamooli sa reh jaata,Mujhko mera sangraam na milta.Gali agar na chunta ye toh, mujhko itna naam na milta. Chandrajeet Singh Rajawat

NEW DELHI: "Shahr mashhoor-e-zamana dekhne aaya hoon main / Rajdhani teri raana dekhne aaya hoon main / Khushnuma jheelon mein larzaan jin ka hai aks-e-jameel / Un haseen mahalon ka naqsha dekhne aaya hoon main. " (I have come to see this city, famed the world over / I have come to see your radiant capital / Whose beautiful reflection trembles in these joyous lakes / I have come to see the design of those beautiful palaces.)These lines, penned by Jaikrishn Chaudhri "Habeeb" in his nazm "Udaipur", encapsulate the essence of a land popularly known as the City of Lakes, the Kashmir of Rajasthan, the Venice of the East, and the White City.Chandrajeet Singh Rajawat is one from those alleys. Today, he represents the city of Udaipur through the game of chess, mentoring students from India and across the globe and also nurturing tutors who can guide and inspire the next generation of aspiring minds.But the road that got him there ran through railway platforms, stolen phone, and a stretch of years when he genuinely did not know where he would sleep that night.Chess wasn't Rajawat's first competitive love. He would play cricket at the district level as a boy. However, drawn to the selection battles and the grind of team competition, he eventually stepped away from the sport.By his teens, he was in the science stream, preparing for the IIT entrance exams, a fairly conventional trajectory for an ambitious Indian teenager, until a Nintendo cartridge got in the way."I had somehow got one of those Mario games," 19960bRajawat told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. There, he stumbled upon something similar to the game of 64 squares. However, his interest in it deepened only after his father took it up."My father started playing it too. I asked him how it was played, and he said, 'This isn't a children's game, you won't understand it,'" he recalled. That single dismissive line lit something in him.He figured the game out on his own, using nothing but the in-game instructions, and beat his father the very next day. Soon, his brief video game obsession fizzled out. But something about that appetite for a genuine intellectual fight didn't.It resurfaced properly around 2011-12, when he attended his first chess tournament and, in his own words, "really fell in love with chess"."It was a game in which I couldn't become good easily. You couldn't easily beat people. That challenge attracted me," he admitted.He was about 16, unusually late by competitive chess standards, but he improved fast. A rough first tournament, a better second, and by his third or fourth event, an outright win that made him Udaipur's player to watch.He'd sit outside tournament halls between rounds, studying by observing stronger players. Despite the noticeable improvement, with his preparation for the IIT entrance exam impacted, his parents grew worried. At one event, one of them pulled him aside and told him plainly to abandon chess and focus on his studies.He started attending tournaments in secret instead. "Whenever I won, the local newspaper would publish the news with my photo," he said, "I would get caught and scolded by my parents."The turning point arrived with his entrance exam results, a rank high enough that, for his family, it represented the kind of opportunity that doesn't come twice.As the eldest son, the expectation was obvious. Rajawat had other plans."I had already decided I would come back to chess," he said. When it came time to fill out his IIT counselling forms, he simply didn't sit for it.His family's financial footing was modest as his father ran a business that operated "somewhat on and off," and the household got by on average means until his mother, previously a homemaker, sat for a government teaching exam and got selected, giving the family a more stable footing.His parents, Gunwanti Rajawat and Vivek Singh Rajawat, were not chess people themselves, and they were not on board with their son's decision."They were extremely upset," Rajawat said. "But I was a little obsessive about it. I always told them, 'It's okay whatever problems you think there are, I'll handle it.'"After a string of arguments, he, unable to find any solution, finally left home with a handful of belongings, still a teenager, with no real plan beyond the board.After leaving home, he arrived in New Delhi alone. And the reason he had left home, chess, did not offer an easy beginning.Even getting into his first FIDE-rated tournament proved difficult, as a dispute over his eligibility with the AICF, India’s chess federation, meant officials initially told him he would not be allowed to play. It was a dispute he says he still does not fully understand. By then, however, he had already sacrificed his safety net to make the trip.He eventually found his way into a Rs 3,500-entry tournament in Delhi in 2014, one that at least came with shared accommodation, because otherwise, in his words, "I didn't even have a place to stay."He gradually started playing well enough to start representing Rajasthan regularly on the national circuit. The years that followed tested him in ways Udaipur never had. His phone was stolen. He slept at stadiums between tournaments, on trains, occasionally on the road, because there simply wasn't money for anything more."I had money for food, but not much beyond that," he said.Asked whether he ever considered going home, his answer was: "No, never. Today, when I look back, all of this seems like a struggle, and people think it sounds like a struggle. But for me, I was actually enjoying it, because I was playing chess."The hinge point in Rajawat's story is a tournament in Delhi that nearly broke him before it made him.Travelling back from the Under-25 Nationals in Chennai, riding the general compartment because there was no money for anything better, his phone was stolen on the train. He ran to the next station and begged officials to check."A phone doesn't just get found like that," they told him.Despite losing the phone, he kept going, scraping by on prize money, until one event nearly broke him psychologically instead.In a tournament in New Delhi, he went on to win several early games. And consequently, he grew overconfident and then lost to a much lower-rated opponent."I thought, what am I doing? If I win, I have no one here to celebrate with," he said.For about two minutes, he seriously considered going home for good, then decided to just play out the three remaining rounds first.He won the next two. In the third, he arrived late, 28 minutes into a 30-minute default window, to face a far more experienced senior player, an Air Force competitor he remembers fondly. His lateness had already cost him most of his clock."I had only about one minute left, while he had around an hour," Rajawat said. It wasn't first place at stake, but prize money significant enough to keep his whole journey alive."Now I have nothing to lose. If I win, something could change."What followed was pure survival chess, thirty-second increments trading down to the wire, until Rajawat held on to win. "After that I felt, now I can do anything," he said. "That was where my journey really began."Word spread quickly that he was a resourceful player who could win from losing positions. He earned the Arena Grandmaster (AGM) title, Rajasthan's first, and began beating FIDE-rated Grandmasters outright, and crossed paths over the board with a young Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa, and Nihal Sarin, long before any of them were famous.Around the same time, he picked up a college seat in mathematics, mostly for formality, at Delhi University (DU). Though, it didn't last for long. Between tournaments, travel, and the demands of practicals and attendance, college quickly became the thing he was least invested in.By then he'd already lived through enough on his own to feel fully independent of the structure a degree was supposed to provide.It was around this same window, toward the end of 2015, still technically enrolled at DU, that he started teaching chess informally around Delhi; someone had mentioned to him that coaching could actually be a source of income, rather than something that only ate into his time.He built it up gradually through 2016, taking on students wherever he could find them, commuting across the city to teach. By 2017-18, that informal teaching had turned into real institutional work, eventually landing him a post at the British School.The early years were still a grind, bouncing between friends' places, then renting a room from an uncle on credit."The first three or four years were a huge struggle," he said. "Then I realised what had seemed extremely difficult from the outside wasn't necessarily impossible."By 2019, restless in Delhi and hearing that Rajasthan wasn't doing enough for chess, he returned home and started a chess academy named Kingdom of Chess, teaching up to 100 students himself.The results followed with his students securing state and national titles, Commonwealth, Asian golds, and a World Championship medal."I realised I could teach 100 children alone, but never thousands," he said. This was the moment that pushed him towards not only teaching children directly but also training the trainers who could. Now, the academy operates in around 30 countries globally. Besides creating awareness about the game, it is also building employment opportunities.Nonetheless, before any of this was certain, there was a teenager who'd just walked out of his family home with nothing guaranteed.Before leaving home in 2014, though, Rajawat wrote a poem, not for an audience, but for a future version of himself."I wrote it for my future self," he said. "I thought that if I ever achieved something, I'd be able to look back at what I had written."
Article Summary: Chandrajeet Singh Rajawat is one of Rajasthan's first AGM. He represents the city of Udaipur through the game of chess. He is also mentoring students from across the globe. He has taught the likes of Yash Bharadia and Arun kataria.

However, neither has publicly confirmed that they have ended their relationship.The breakup rumors surrounding AJ Smith-Shawver and Josie Canseco began after fans noticed changes to both of their Instagram accounts. A six-time Pro Bowler , reduced to a shorts discourse

Forget the joint practice takeaways. Forget Justin Herbert torching San Francisco's secondary. On Tuesday, the only thing NFL Twitter wanted to talk about was Mike Evans' shorts.An account posted a harmless six-second clip captionedWhat it actually delivered was Evans, all 6'5" and 231 pounds of him, in compression shorts so short and so tight that half the internet forgot football was being played at all. The quote-tweet that sent it flying was a simpleThis wasn't a one-tweet fluke. NFL insiders and fans got in on it too, declaring the moment officially trending and joking that Evans was fullySome accounts flagged it as a trending topic in its own right, noting Evans had gone viral purely over his wardrobe since the move to San Francisco.Even Deebo Samuel, who was standing right next to Evans in the clip, got dragged into it. One account's caption zeroed in on both of them, joking that something was clearly "goin on out here" with the shorts situation in San Francisco.Then came the memes. One account paired the clip with a side-by-side of a classic comedy-movie gag involving two grown men in tiny matching red shorts, captioning it as Evans and quarterback Brock Purdy "after connecting on a 15-yard pass." It's the kind of joke that only works because the visual is just that specific.What Evans is actually wearing is standard football compression gear, tight base-layer shorts players wear under their pants for support and to prevent muscle strains. For one afternoon, the biggest story out of 49ers training camp wasn't Justin Herbert torching San Francisco's secondary or Christian McCaffrey's mystery injury; it was a Hall of Fame-caliber wideout accidentally becoming the day's funniest meme. Football is a business of routes and coverages. The internet, given the choice, will always choose the shorts.The 49ers and Chargers face off in their second preseason game tonight. Evans' outfit for that one remains, mercifully, the standard uniform.

Article Title: Khabib Nurmagomedov’s yet another old clip about Islam Makhachev’s potential goes viral, his 2018 warning to Gleison Tibau looks prophetic years later

Islam Makhachev (Image via UFC)

Anatomy of a Fighter

Khabib Nurmagomedov’s warning about Islam Makhachev came true against Gleison Tibau

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before Islam Makhachev became a two-division UFC champion, Khabib Nurmagomedov was already convinced his teammate was special. In behind-the-scenes footage from 2018, Nurmagomedov issued a blunt warning ahead of Makhachev’s fight with Gleison Tibau.The throwback footage, shared by filmmaker Will Harris as part of, captured Nurmagomedov speaking about Makhachev before the Brazilian veteran faced him. Makhachev was still developing his reputation at the time. But Nurmagomedov believed he was already operating at a completely different level.Khabib Nurmagomedov’s comment came ahead of Islam Makhachev’s fifth UFC appearance. The Russian star was already highly respected for his wrestling and grappling. He also knew Makhachev better than most. The two trained together under Khabib’s late father and coach, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov.That made Nurmagomedov’s prediction particularly interesting.Gleison Tibau was an experienced UFC veteran. He had fought some of the biggest names in the lightweight division. For a young Makhachev, the matchup represented another important step in his UFC career.Nurmagomedov, however, did not appear concerned.“Sorry Tibau, but Islam is different level, be careful brother”, he said in the viral clip.The message was simple. Nurmagomedov believed Makhachev’s skills were too advanced for Tibau.Makhachev then provided an emphatic answer inside the Octagon.At UFC 220, he stopped Tibau in just 57 seconds of the first round. The result was a knockout win and another major step forward in his career.At that stage, few could have known how far Makhachev would eventually go. The lightweight contender later became one of the most dominant fighters in UFC history.Makhachev won the vacant UFC lightweight championship at UFC 280 in 2022. He submitted Charles Oliveira to capture the title. He then successfully defended it four times.His success eventually took him into a second weight division.Makhachev moved up to welterweight and captured another UFC championship by defeating Jack Della Maddalena. He later defended the welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330.His run also saw him break the UFC record for consecutive victories. His winning streak reached 17 fights, moving him past Anderson Silva’s previous mark of 16 consecutive UFC wins.Nurmagomedov has remained one of Makhachev’s biggest supporters throughout the journey.After Makhachev reached the record, Khabib praised his longtime friend and teammate on social media.“There is a word : Achievement. Article Title: Who was Leroy Saunders? All about Leroy Saunders, the fitness coach who died after collapsing at HYROX event in Bangkok

Who was Leroy Saunders?

Leroy Saunders passed away after collapsing at HYROX Bangkok event

South African fitness coach Leroy Saunders has died at the age of 41 after collapsing during the BYD HYROX Bangkok 2026 competition. Saunders lost consciousness while competing at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center on August 13. Event staff and medical personnel immediately began CPR and emergency resuscitation.He was then taken to a hospital, where he later died. His family and social-media team confirmed his death on August 18. However, they have not revealed a cause of death and have asked people not to speculate about the circumstances.Leroy Saunders was a South African fitness coach who was based in Bangkok, Thailand. He built a career around fitness, strength and conditioning.Saunders was the owner of IAOT CrossFit in Bangkok. The gym is listed in CrossFit’s official affiliate directory. Through his work there, he became known among Thailand’s CrossFit and functional-fitness communities.He was also connected to the combat-sports world. Saunders founded Fight by Design, a strength and conditioning system designed to help combat athletes prepare for competition.The programme worked with athletes from several disciplines.These included Muay Thai, mixed martial arts and boxing.Saunders focused on areas such as strength, movement, durability and physical performance. His work was aimed at helping fighters become stronger and better prepared for the demands of competition.He was also a trained functional-fitness athlete himself. Saunders had previously competed in HYROX events. In 2025, he took part in a HYROX doubles event with Annika Saunders. The pair completed the race in 1 hour, 17 minutes and 51 seconds.HYROX combines running with eight functional workout stations. Competitors can take part in individual, doubles or relay categories. The Bangkok event was held from August 13 to 16.Saunders was competing in the event when he suddenly collapsed and lost consciousness on August 13.Medical personnel and event staff responded quickly. CPR and emergency resuscitation were carried out at the venue. Leroy Saunders was then transported to hospital for further treatment. He later died.His official Instagram account confirmed the tragic news.“Last Thursday, we unfortunately lost Leroy due to reasons we are still trying to fully understand,” the statement said.The statement also thanked the many people who sent messages and offered support following Saunders’ death.His family and team said the response showed the positive impact he had on people around him.They described Saunders as someone who lived without regret or hesitation. They said he encouraged “hundreds, if not thousands” of others to do the same.His social-media team, IRONSPRT, will manage future posts on his official account. The team will do so in consultation with and with the approval of his closest family and friends.Further details are expected about plans to celebrate Saunders’ life and remember him in a way that would make him proud.The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. His family has asked for privacy and patience while they seek answers.
Article Summary: Leroy Saunders was a South African fitness coach who was based in Bangkok. He built a career around fitness, strength and conditioning. Saunders lost consciousness while competing at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center on August 13. Event staff and medical personnel immediately began CPR and emergency resuscitation. He was then taken to a hospital, where he later died.
