Article Title: Hockey World Cup: India extend dominance over Pakistan with 5-3 thriller, seal next-round spot
Article Text:
India beat Pakistan (Pic credit: Hockey India)

As it happened:

Harmanpreet, Abhishek put India in command

Pakistan fight back in goal-filled second quarter

Hardik restores three-goal cushion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan threaten late, but India hold firm

NEW DELHI: India extended their dominance over arch-rivals Pakistan with a thrilling 5-3 victory in their final Pool D match of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup on Wednesday, overcoming a spirited fightback to book their place in the next round.In a contest befitting one of hockey's biggest rivalries, India raced to a 3-0 lead before Pakistan repeatedly threatened a comeback. Harmanpreet Singh and Abhishek scored twice each, while Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke as India maintained their grip on the contest.Pakistan fought back through Hannan Shahid's brace and Sufyan Khan's penalty-corner strike, but India held their nerve during a tense final quarter, including a spell when they were reduced to 10 players.India finished second in Pool D with six points from three matches, behind England, who topped the group with nine points. Pakistan were eliminated.India made a flying start and were rewarded with their first penalty corner in the fifth minute. Harmanpreet's initial drag-flick struck a Pakistan defender's foot, but the India captain got another opportunity and made no mistake.He kept his second effort low and hard towards the goalkeeper's left, beating the post defender to put India ahead.India doubled their advantage in the 11th minute. Abhishek showed excellent control to bring down an aerial ball before playing it across goal, with the ball eventually finding the net off a Pakistan stick. The goal was initially credited to Mandeep Singh during the live action, but the FIH website later credited it to Abhishek.India continued to dominate possession and territory, with much of the play taking place in Pakistan's half. The hosts went into the first-quarter break with a 2-0 advantage.Harmanpreet then struck again in the 21st minute, this time following a penalty-corner variation. Rajinder Singh took the initial drag-flick, which was saved, but India retained possession and Harmanpreet hammered the rebound past the goalkeeper.The goal took Harmanpreet's tally to five at the 2026 World Cup.Pakistan refused to fold and immediately pulled one back through Hannan Shahid in the 22nd minute. Suraj made the initial save, but Hannan reacted quickest to the rebound and beat the goalkeeper at the second attempt.India restored their three-goal cushion almost immediately. Abhishek produced a superb individual move inside the circle, showing excellent dribbling skills before his effort took a deflection off a Pakistan stick and found the net.Pakistan responded once again. Sufyan Khan converted a penalty corner in the 25th minute, with his drag-flick taking a deflection off Amit Rohidas before ending up in the goal.The second quarter had produced four goals and turned the contest into an increasingly frantic affair. India went into half-time with a 4-2 advantage, but Pakistan had shown they were capable of causing problems.India regained some breathing space early in the second half when they were awarded a penalty stroke after an intentional foul inside the circle. Hardik Singh stepped up and made no mistake, sending the ball into the net to restore India's three-goal advantage.Pakistan continued to push forward, but India defended several dangerous moments effectively. The visitors also earned a penalty corner on the counter-attack, only for India's rushing defenders to put enough pressure on the drag-flicker to force the effort wide.India remained in control heading into the final quarter, although Abhishek came close to adding another before his effort struck the side netting.Pakistan made the perfect start to the final quarter when Hannan Shahid scored his second goal in the 46th minute. Pakistan won possession after Hardik lost the ball in midfield, and Hannan produced a composed finish to cut India's lead to 5-3.India were increasingly forced to defend as Pakistan pressed high in search of another opening. The pressure intensified when Aditya Arjun was shown a yellow card, leaving India with 10 players for the final five minutes.Pakistan won a penalty-corner referral after the ball was adjudged to have hit the shin guard of an Indian defender and continued throwing players forward. India, however, defended resolutely and refused to surrender their two-goal advantage.The result extended India's strong recent dominance over Pakistan and ensured they advanced to the next round of the World Cup, while Pakistan's campaign came to an end.
Article Summary: India beat Pakistan 5-3 in their final Pool D match of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup. Harmanpreet Singh and Abhishek scored twice each, while Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke. Pakistan fought back through Hannan Shahid's brace and Sufyan Khan's penalty-corner strike, but India held their nerve.

Article Title: Olivia Culpo flaunts her baby bump in a skin-tight black outfit at 49ers practice while Christian McCaffrey watches from the sidelines
Article Text:
Christian McCaffrey, Olivia Culpo

Olivia Culpo flaunts baby bump in black bodysuit as Christian McCaffrey's injury mystery deepens

A confident display amid contract rumors

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

that

Christian McCaffrey couldn't practice on Tuesday. His wife didn't need to say a word to steal the moment anyway. Olivia Culpo showed up to the 49ers-Chargers joint session in El Segundo in a skin-tight black bodysuit and leggings, baby bump front and center, standing beside Christian's parents and his brother Max, the Chargers' new running backs coach, while Christian himself watched from the sidelines in street clothes. It was a full family affair. It was also, whether she meant it that way or not, a distraction from the one question the 49ers still won't answer.Culpo, 34 and expecting baby number two with McCaffrey, didn't dress like someone trying to blend into a practice-field crowd. The black sleeveless bodysuit hugged every inch of her growing bump, paired with matching leggings and slides. Simple, but it did exactly what it was supposed to do. She stood side by side with Christian's mom Lisa and his sister-in-law, both in soft neutral tones, which made Olivia's all-black moment pop even harder in the group shot Lisa later posted.This is Culpo's second pregnancy since marrying McCaffrey in 2024. She announced it in early May, just months after their daughter Colette turned one. And she's made a habit this pregnancy of not hiding the bump with beach shots, crop tops, now this.Say what you want about WAG culture, but there's something almost defiant about a woman who keeps showing up in fitted everything while pregnant, like she's decided the bump is the outfit, not something to work around.Christian didn't participate in Tuesday's practice at all. He's been out for days with what Kyle Shanahan is only calling "tightness," and no further explanation, which in NFL speak usually means either something worse than they're letting on, or a very deliberate non-answer.Pro Football Talk floated a theory that it's contract-related, that McCaffrey might be posturing for a pay bump after Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs reset the running back market this offseason. Shanahan shot that down publicly. McCaffrey showed up, watched, then posed for family photos afterward, which, fair or not, is exactly the kind of image that fuels more speculation, not less.There's something almost strategic about how visible Olivia was in that moment. Maybe it's nothing; maybe she just wanted family photos with her mother-in-law before a big joint practice. But when your husband is the center of an injury-or-contract guessing game, and you show up looking like, cameras are going to find you regardless.It shifted the day's headlines from "why isn't McCaffrey practicing" to "Olivia Culpo's bump" at least for a news cycle. Whether that's convenient or coincidental is the kind of thing only the McCaffreys know.Either way, the 49ers and Chargers play their second preseason matchup tonight, and McCaffrey is expected to sit again. Culpo, bump and all, will probably be there watching. She usually is.
Article Summary: Olivia Culpo showed up to the 49ers-Chargers joint session in El Segundo in a skin-tight black bodysuit and leggings. She stood beside Christian's parents and his brother Max, the Chargers' new running backs coach, while Christian himself watched from the sidelines.

Article Title: Valkyrae’s AI controversy grows as streamer reveals the artist behind her disputed YouTube thumbnail
Article Text:
Valkyrae addresses AI allegations over YouTube thumbnail

Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko

Rachell “Valkyrae” Hofstetter has addressed a growing debate over the artwork used for her YouTube livestreams after viewers accused her latest thumbnail of being AI-generated. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, Anko, while admitting she understands why some people reached that conclusion. Her comments also highlight a wider concern for digital artists as AI-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.The controversy began after Anko, Valkyrae’s thumbnail artist, shared the creative process behind artwork for her Uncharted playthrough. The thumbnail initially received attention from viewers, but some quickly questioned whether artificial intelligence had been used to create it.That reaction eventually reached Valkyrae, who explained that Anko creates all of her YouTube livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his process online. She also pointed out the irony of the situation, saying that even those behind-the-scenes videos have not stopped people from making AI accusations.Valkyrae said:"Okay. We have to talk about this thumbnail debacle. I don't know what to do about this thumbnail debacle.So, as most of you know, every single one of my YouTube livestream thumbnails is made by the same artist. His name is Anko, and he makes all of them. He even posts on Twitter the art process of making them, but it still never beats the AI allegations. And the most recent thumbnail, he makes new thumbnails when I start a new game series, so, obviously, there is a new thumbnail for the Uncharted era. And people were saying, 'Oh, it's AI slop,' in the pre-chat."The streamer then offered a more nuanced response. Rather than dismissing viewers who suspected AI, she said she understood where their reaction came from. At the same time, she wanted to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI.Valkyrae added:"'Just ignore them.' Well, no. Okay? I don't blame people for thinking it's AI because AI is using people's art, like Anko's, to take over. But I would like to clear it up because there were a few people that were saying, 'Oh! When I saw the thumb, I also thought it was AI.' So now I am wondering how many people are out there that would watch the stream, but didn't because of the AI-looking thumbnail! But it's not AI."The discussion also became personal for Valkyrae because she said she felt bad for Anko. The thumbnail was later updated, with the artist adding his signature, giving viewers another indication of who created the work.Valkyrae explained that the situation made her think about the broader impact AI tools could have on working artists. For creators who depend on commissioned digital artwork, being mistaken for AI-generated work can create a difficult problem. The visual style that once helped an artist stand out can now cause audiences to question whether a human created it at all.She said:"I don't know, dude. I don't know what to do about it. I feel bad for him, though, because... and then, it, like, reminded me. I was like, 'Man, I just shouldn't do art thumbnails.' But then, the whole AI thing is doing what it does - making artists lose their jobs! Isn't that crazy?!"The controversy has now become more than a discussion about one YouTube thumbnail. Valkyrae’s response reflects a growing tension between AI-generated imagery and human-made digital art, particularly on social media where polished artwork can be judged within seconds.For Valkyrae, however, the message is straightforward: the Uncharted thumbnail was made by Anko, not AI. The debate instead shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.
Article Summary: Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko after viewers accuse him of being AI- generated. The streamer says she understands where people are coming from, but wants to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI. The debate shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.

Former Chicago Cubs outfielder Jason Heyward is enjoying more time away from baseball after ending his 16-year MLB career earlier this year. The retired All-Star recently shared a relaxed summer moment with his wife, Vedrana, during a yacht outing. Vedrana posted pictures from the trip on her Instagram Story, including a photo of the couple together and another showing her feet in the water. She captioned one post, “Hey babe,” and wrote, “Love you summertime chi,” on another. The outing comes as Heyward begins a new chapter with the Los Angeles Dodgers.Vedrana Heyward gave followers a small look at their time on the water this week. In one Instagram Story, she posed with Jason Heyward while wearing a brown bikini. Another picture showed the view from the yacht as she relaxed with her feet in the water.The posts offered a simple look at the couple's life away from the baseball field. Heyward and Vedrana have been married since March 2021 and have two children, Messi and Slaš. Their family life has mostly stayed away from the spotlight, although Vedrana has supported Heyward throughout his playing career.She has also built work of her own through. The program was launched alongside the Jason Heyward Baseball Academy and focuses on giving young women opportunities through sports, mentorship and leadership.The program is part of the couple's wider effort to support young people in Chicago.Heyward's retirement became official in March 2026.reported that he announced the decision on March 27 after 16 seasons in the majors. He finished his career as a five-time Gold Glove winner, an All-Star and a two-time World Series champion. His first championship came with the Cubs in 2016.Retirement did not keep Jason Heyward away from baseball for long. In May, thereported that the Dodgers brought him back as a special assistant in their front office.Heyward said he wanted to learn more about the business side of baseball. His new duties include taking part in draft meetings, meeting new players and spending time around the team's affiliates. He can also return to the clubhouse and share his experience with players and staff.The role gives Heyward a chance to learn how a team works beyond the field. He told the Los Angeles Times that he hopes to keep learning about scouting, player evaluation, research and analytics as he moves toward the next part of his career.Heyward's final playing season came with the San Diego Padres in 2025. He played 34 games before finishing his 16-year career. Before that, he spent the biggest part of his career with the Cubs from 2016 through 2022. He also played for the Atlanta Braves, St. Louis Cardinals, Dodgers and Houston Astros.For now, Heyward has both baseball and family life keeping him busy. His yacht outing with Vedrana offered a brief glimpse of the quieter side of that new chapter.

Article Title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning
Article Text:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen (Getty Images)

Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce

Gisele Bündchen focuses on her children after divorce

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the supermodel went through after their marriage ended. During a conversation with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Bündchen struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage, her children and the new chapter she was trying to build.The interview, released in March 2024 as part of “IMPACT x Nightline: Gisele Bündchen: Climbing the Mountain,” came more than a year after Bündchen and Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022.Their split ended a relationship that had lasted 16 years and a marriage that had lasted 13. By the time Bündchen sat down with Roberts, however, she was trying to understand the experience as part of a larger personal transition rather than simply an ending.Roberts reminded her that she had previously described the divorce as “the death of a dream.” The comment immediately struck an emotional chord.“Well, when you say ...” the model began, before pausing and getting teary. “Sorry, guys, I didn't know ... can I have a little moment?”After collecting herself, Bündchen spoke about accepting a future she had never expected to have.“It's definitely a time of, you know, a transition that had to take place, and it's not something that you — I don't think you wish for that, you know?” she said. “But I think sometimes in life things happen. I feel so blessed because, like, I wouldn't change anything in my life. I had incredible experiences. I learned so much. I have my children, which are the biggest blessings in my life.“And now I get to create — it's a new season, a new chapter in my life, and I get to learn new things, and I get to walk my path in a different way, you know?“And I'm grateful for all of it. I'm grateful for every lesson.”Her words showed that the divorce was not something she viewed in simple terms. There was pain, but there was also gratitude for the years she shared with Brady and the family they created.Bündchen and Brady share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has a son, Jack, with actress Bridget Moynahan. For Bündchen, co-parenting meant accepting that the children would grow up moving between two different households and sets of rules.“There's easier days than others. But it's amazing that the kids — they're super smart children,” Bündchen said, laughing. “They know what they can get away with. So I think it's natural that it has different rules, and kids just adapt and they're going to try to do what they want. And I can only control what I do.”She also emphasized the value of her children having relationships with both parents.“It's amazing that they get to spend time with both parents because it's more enriching for their lives, two different worlds, and they get to learn from two different worlds.”Bündchen spoke warmly about Brady’s oldest son, Jack, whom she helped raise during her years with the former NFL star.“I raised him. I love him,” she said.Looking ahead, Bündchen said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.“I'm very committed to living my truth more than ever, so I would say that's where my heart is now, where I am right now. I'm living my truth and I'm not apologizing for it,” she explained.The 2024 interview remains significant because it captured Bündchen at a vulnerable point in her life. She was not simply discussing a famous divorce. She was describing the difficult process of accepting change, protecting her children and finding an identity beyond a marriage that had once shaped so much of her public life.
Article Summary: Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022. The supermodel struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage. She said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
Article Text:
Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE. Their current net-worth estimates vary significantly across sources and should be treated cautiously because personal assets, debts, taxes, expenses and private income are not fully disclosed.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number. The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling- related projects.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015

Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.On Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct.10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham started a GoFundMe page to raise money for fines or a yacht. The Indiana Fever guard then chose to give the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities. Cunningham first encountered the charity as a teenager during a McDonald's All-American Game.

Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
